recommendation: Keep the audit commit. Future changes to this behavior should be made in org.hl7.fhir.core/validator code; only a new work-group decision should add normative year-range guidance to the FHIR specification itself.
issue_request: The Published/Persuasive with Modification Jira asked to address InstanceValidator.yearIsValid(), which rejected date/dateTime/instant years outside 1800..2100 even though the FHIR primitive regexes do not impose that range. The final decision was to keep the reasonable-year validation but report it as a warning instead of an error.
initial_application: Jira records Grahame Grieve's linked org.hl7.fhir.core commit 0477bf174e44583ea4c227ad9d37756789ccba9c. That external commit changes InstanceValidator dateTime, date, and instant year checks from rule(...) errors to warning(...) diagnostics and updates the message to describe an outside-reasonable-years data-entry warning.
additional_context: The 2019 Zulip thread and FHIR-I minutes both support the same result: very old or future dates can be suspicious without being invalid FHIR. The current HL7/fhir checkout has no Java source files and no yearIsValid or reasonable-year diagnostic text, while the current external validator source still uses warning(...) for the reasonable-year check.
reconciliation: No HL7/fhir source change was made. The issue belongs to external validator implementation code that has already been updated, and the current spec source contains no contradictory normative date-year restriction to remove or revise.
